scene: Two black-outline stick figures stand either side of a small wheeled cart under a fringed umbrella; the left figure has an exclamation mark beside its head and holds a flat rectangular object, the right figure wears a cap and holds a bun-like shape over the cart. About five red banknote scribbles flutter above the cart. The frame is a vertical image pillarboxed with blurred grey bars.
mechanism: A giant numeric figure sits above a hot-dog-stand scene, so the question of what all that money could buy is posed through an everyday street purchase.
composition: The artwork occupies only the centre column of the frame, about a third of its width, with the two figures framing the cart and umbrella in a symmetrical triangle. The number runs along the top edge and the lower fifth is empty white. Grey side bars add dead space and shrink everything.
typography: One long numeric string of thin hand-lettered black digits runs across the top of the white column, only about as wide as the column. At 160x90 the digits are a thin smudge, so the magnitude cannot be read; the title adds the all-the-world's-money framing the image lacks.
colors: Black line art on near-white paper with a single red accent for the flying notes, set against flat mid-grey side bars. Red is used only for the money, so it marks the one coloured idea; the overall palette is very low in saturation.
psychology: The stick figures have blank oval faces with no visible expression; the exclamation mark by the left head and the airborne notes are the only cues of surprise or spending. No authority or fear cue is visible.
partnership: The title poses a what-if about owning all the world's money; the thumbnail answers with a specific trillion-scale figure in a vending context, which complements rather than repeats it. The open question is what the stand sale shows, and the number itself may satisfy part of the curiosity.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the long number at top first, then the red notes, then the umbrella and cart, then the two figures.
art: Loose hand-drawn marker doodle with wobbly uneven line weight, flat fills and no shading. The execution is deliberately rough and coherent, but the strong vertical crop leaves roughly two thirds of the canvas as grey padding.
strength: A single big number gives an immediate scale hook above a simple, recognisable street-stand scene.
weakness: Thin line art and the digits shrink to a faint blur at phone size, and the grey pillarbox wastes most of the frame.
bottleneck: The key information, the number, is the smallest-contrast element in the frame.
action: Hypothesis: render the figure as $10 TRILLION in heavy letters across the full 16:9 frame to test whether a readable magnitude lifts glanceability.
counterexample: Seq 19 puts a $100 BILLION amount in heavy yellow capitals over a money pile, where this thumbnail's number is a thin line.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: What is atrial fibrillation? / Atrial Fibrillation / THE LOWER CHAMBER SQUEEZES, / Cara Pellegrini, MD / Leslie Kernisan, MD MPH / [BetterHealthWhileAging.net] / [BruceBlaus https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki File:Atrial_Fibrillation.png]
scene: A vertical screen-capture layout on a teal-grey blurred background: a teal header band holds a question, below it an anatomical heart drawing sits beside two black ECG strips, one with evenly spaced spikes and one with irregular spikes. Under a caption bar are two stacked video-call frames, the upper a woman with wavy hair raising a hand near her face and the lower a smiling woman with dark curly hair, each with a teal name tag. A teal footer band carries a web address.
mechanism: An explainer card stacking a labelled heart diagram, a regular-versus-irregular ECG pair and two speaker frames, so the format promises a definition delivered by named doctors.
composition: A centred portrait column takes about a third of the width with side areas filled by blurred teal. Stacked bands run top to bottom: header, diagram, caption bar, two speaker frames, footer. No single focal point wins; the heart drawing and the two speaker frames compete at similar visual weight.
typography: Roughly eighteen words appear in several sizes, the question header and the caption bar being the largest. The tiny image-credit lines and the footer address are unreadable at 160x90, and the question header repeats the title almost word for word.
colors: Teal bands and a teal-grey background around a white card, with red, purple and tan heart tones and black ECG panels with pale green traces. Colours are soft and low in contrast; nothing is coded as a warning.
psychology: The upper speaker raises a hand near the face with her mouth slightly open; the lower speaker has a closed-mouth smile. Medical credentials (MD, MD MPH) printed on name tags are the main authority cue.
partnership: The top band repeats the title question, so the thumbnail adds no new promise beyond showing a diagram and two named speakers. The caption fragment ending in a comma is mid-sentence and raises an unanswered thought rather than a clear hook.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the teal header question first, then the heart drawing and ECG strips, then the caption bar, then the two speaker frames.
art: A composite of a Wikimedia-style anatomical drawing, vector ECG panels and two webcam-style video frames with inconsistent lighting between them (a bright window behind one speaker, a plain wall behind the other); the pieces are clearly stitched but not deceptively blended. Every element is small inside the narrow column.
strength: Named MD credentials and a clear labelled heart-plus-ECG illustration make the topic and source immediately understandable.
weakness: Content is crowded into a narrow column, so the speaker faces and diagram detail are tiny and the caption fragment is mid-sentence.
bottleneck: Too many equal-weight bands leave no dominant element to hold attention in a feed.
action: Hypothesis: keep only the irregular ECG strip and one enlarged speaker face with the question in 16:9, to test whether removing the stack improves focus.
counterexample: Seq 23 has a similar caption-plus-speaker format but far less text, which shows how much simpler this layout could be.
medical_notes: The packaging is a neutral definition question with named MD credentials and a labelled diagram, making no cure or diagnosis claim.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A huge cartoon long-necked dinosaur head fills the left and centre, with a red-veined bulging eye, thin red streaks running from the eye and from a wide-open mouth showing two rows of teeth and a pink tongue. Green vines wind around the neck and purple patches mark the skin. A thin hand-drawn curved arrow beside the text points up toward the head. The background is plain white.
mechanism: An injured, dripping dinosaur head paired with a short note about a physical limit turns the title's complaint into one concrete, uncomfortable fact.
composition: The head and neck sweep diagonally from the lower left up to the upper centre, with the open mouth as the primary focal point. The text sits in the lower right, tied back to the head by a small curved arrow. White negative space around the subject gives clean separation.
typography: Two lines, three words, in thin black hand-lettered capitals, with the second line larger. The words stay legible at 160x90 but have low weight beside the dark-outlined head; they add the specific fact the title only hints at.
colors: Olive-brown body with green vines and purple patches against pure white, plus blood-red streaks from the eye and jaw as the only bright accent. High subject-to-background separation, and the red draws the eye to the face.
psychology: The creature shows wide, bloodshot eyes and a gaping mouth with red streaks, which reads as pain or distress. The gore detail adds a disturbing, morbid cue and a vulnerability angle.
partnership: The title asks why it is bad to be born a brachiosaurus; the thumbnail supplies a specific symptom, the animal cannot lie down, which complements the title. The unanswered question is why it cannot lie down.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red-streaked eye and open mouth first, then the curved arrow, then the two lines of text, then the vine-wrapped neck.
art: Clean cartoon vector with consistent outlines, flat shading and plausible neck proportions. The vines and purple patches read as deliberate decoration; the large white field keeps the image uncluttered and the head survives at mobile size.
strength: One huge face with a single clear symptom caption makes the premise legible instantly.
weakness: The thin lettering is light against the heavy illustration and the gore can read as shock rather than explanation.
bottleneck: The caption is visually weaker than the head, so the specific hook is the second thing read.
action: Hypothesis: thicken the CAN'T LIE DOWN lettering and add a short outline to test whether the caption reads as fast as the eye.
counterexample: Seq 24 shares the white-ground, distressed-animal-head, handwritten-caption layout, but its caption gives a statistic where this one names a symptom.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A night forest scene with a crescent moon at upper right. A white-headed stick figure with dot eyes and a flat mouth kneels at left and holds a splintered stick against the paw of a brown canine lying on the grass; the paw shows a red wound. The canine looks down at the paw with wide, slightly raised eyes. A small campfire burns at the bottom centre and green bushes frame both sides.
mechanism: A tender rescue moment, a figure treating a wounded canine's paw, makes the question about animal awareness concrete and emotionally readable.
composition: The stick figure and canine form a left-to-right pair in the lower middle with the paw as the meeting point, and the fire anchors the bottom. The headline spans the top fifth. Dark blue sky in the centre isolates the white head, though the trees and bushes add layered mid-ground detail.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a dark outline run across nearly the full width at the top, and they stay crisp at 160x90. The headline is a shortened form of the title question and adds no new noun; the helping action comes from the scene.
colors: Deep navy sky and green foliage with a bright yellow headline, a white head and a warm orange fire. Yellow-on-dark gives strong text contrast, and the red wound is a small accent with only local meaning.
psychology: The canine has wide eyes and a downward glance at the wound, while the stick figure has a flat neutral face. The visible cues read as vulnerability and care rather than threat.
partnership: The title asks whether animals know humans are helping, and the thumbnail shows exactly that scenario, so it complements the title by adding the visual evidence. The unanswered question is the animal's reaction, which the eyes only partly hint at.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the white round head, then the canine's eyes and paw, then the fire.
art: Flat illustrated style with a stick figure placed into a more detailed, shaded canine and forest, giving a slight stylistic mismatch between subject and background; the forest layering is busy but reads clearly. Lighting is consistently night-toned.
strength: A clear before-the-answer scene with high-contrast yellow text delivers the question in one glance.
weakness: Forest layers and the plain stick face keep the emotional focus split between figure and canine.
bottleneck: The paw wound, the central story detail, is small compared with the headline and background.
action: Hypothesis: zoom in on the canine's face and paw and keep the stick figure partially cropped to test whether a tighter shot strengthens the emotional read.
counterexample: Seq 13 uses a similar large-yellow-question headline but over a flat orange scene with less depth.
expression_label: neutral stick face; canine with wide downcast eyes
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A muted beige and grey cartoon scene of a walled compound with tiled-roof pavilions, a closed double gate, a watchtower at right with two tiny figures, and an armoured vehicle in the centre. Six black silhouettes stand around the yard, two at each guard booth and one on each side of the vehicle. A large round-headed cartoon figure with round glasses, a flat mouth, a dark flat-top haircut and a uniform with a medal cluster stands at right with hands behind its back.
mechanism: A ranked-level label placed over a heavily guarded compound frames the title's society hierarchy as a top-tier reveal, the last of a seven-step ladder.
composition: The large uniformed figure on the right takes the closest plane while the gate and vehicle recede left. The quote sits in the top band, and the silhouettes at the edges act as symmetrical flanks. The scene is wide and orderly, with a clear foreground-to-background depth.
typography: Four words in a thin handwritten quote at the top, small relative to the frame, with very low weight against the pale sky. They partly survive at 160x90 but are readable only as a thin line; the quote carries the level number that the title leaves out.
colors: A near-monochrome palette of cream, khaki-grey and olive with black silhouettes; the only colour accent is a tiny red badge on the uniform. Low saturation gives a restrained, bleak mood but little pop against other feed thumbnails.
psychology: The central figure has wide round eyes behind glasses and a flat, closed mouth, a deadpan look; the black silhouettes and guard booths add a surveillance and authority cue. There is no bright urgency signal.
partnership: The title promises a tour of every level of society; the thumbnail shows only the top level, Level Seven, which implies a ladder and complements the title. The unanswered question is what the lower levels look like.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large central uniformed figure first, then the quote at the top, then the gate and vehicle, then the silhouettes.
art: Clean flat cartoon with consistent outline weight and soft grey shading; the figure's oversized head against a detailed, realistic compound is a deliberate style contrast. The background is orderly and the figure separates from it by scale.
strength: The Level Seven label and guarded compound set up a clear ranked-society premise with a distinct visual world.
weakness: The pale, thin quote and washed-out palette reduce impact in a busy feed.
bottleneck: The hook phrase has low contrast and low weight, so the ladder idea is easy to miss.
action: Hypothesis: set Level Seven in heavy black caps with a dark band behind it and add small lower-level silhouettes below, to test whether the ladder concept reads faster.
counterexample: Seq 7 uses the same rank framing but with a heavy red-and-black text hook on white, giving a much stronger text signal.
expression_label: wide eyes behind glasses, flat mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: YOUR FEET WILL TELL / YOUR SUGAR / IS DAMAGING YOU
scene: The photo shows a bare foot with purple-red discolouration and three small dark spots (one near the ankle, two near the heel and arch), framed in a white box with a red outline.
mechanism: A doctor-styled figure pointing at a close-up of a discoloured foot turns a vague threat about sugar into a concrete visible symptom the viewer can self-check.
composition: The headline stack takes the left two thirds and the man's torso and face the right third, with the pointing finger and yellow arrow forming a diagonal to the foot at the bottom. The foot photo is the secondary focus. Black and red panels split the frame cleanly, though the whole image is densely packed.
typography: Nine words in three tiers: yellow YOUR FEET WILL TELL, large white YOUR SUGAR, and white on a red box IS DAMAGING YOU. All three lines stay readable at 160x90. The text names sugar and feet, while the title adds the diagnosis wording, the number nine and the age band.
colors: Black, red and white with a yellow accent for the top line and arrow, a high-alarm scheme. The red box and red backdrop signal danger and urgency, and the foot photo's red border repeats it.
psychology: The man has furrowed brows, a closed, downturned mouth and a direct stare, a serious, concerned look reinforced by scrubs and stethoscope as authority cues. The foot discolouration adds a fear and vulnerability cue.
partnership: The title adds a cardiologist, nine foot signs and the over-60 age marker, while the thumbnail adds a single foot image and a direct you-are-being-damaged claim, so they complement but the thumbnail's one foot does not show nine signs. A cardiology credential against a diabetes foot topic is an unresolved mismatch.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large white YOUR SUGAR first, then the man's stare, then the yellow arrow and foot photo, then the red box.
art: Photo-style portrait with an inset foot photo and overlaid vector arrow; the subject is cleanly cut out against the red backdrop. The foot photo has a white studio background that does not match the frame's lighting, but it is clearly an inset rather than a blend.
strength: A large, direct headline plus a visible foot close-up links a feared symptom to a plain, personal claim.
weakness: Alarmist wording and dramatic discolouration invite a fear read and the single foot does not show the nine signs promised by the title.
bottleneck: The credential suggested by scrubs and the diabetes claim are unsupported on the image alone, which raises trust risk.
action: Hypothesis: replace the damaging-you claim with a neutral question such as FOOT CHANGES TO CHECK and add a text badge for the number 9, to test whether a less alarmist, number-led headline keeps the hook.
counterexample: Seq 10 uses a similar red-black senior-health layout but shows a drinking action with a how-to angle rather than a body-damage claim.
medical_notes: A scrubs-clad presenter and a discoloured foot image with a damage claim imply a diagnosis, while the cardiologist title label does not match a diabetes foot topic on the image alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A side-on cartoon figure in a black helmet, dark goggles and a gas mask aims a suppressed submachine gun toward the left, with a red-marked selector on the receiver. The dark vest carries a white SWAT label and the sleeve has a white cross on a dark shield; a radio antenna rises behind the shoulder. A thin curved arrow from the left of the text points to the gun muzzle. The background is plain white.
mechanism: A first-person-style 'It's you' caption with the muzzle pointing at the arrow draws the viewer into the role, so the title's ranks premise starts with the armed officer.
composition: The figure fills the right half and the gun crosses the middle, with its muzzle at the arrow tip, so the arrow links caption to weapon. Text occupies the upper left above the gun. White space and a dark-on-light contrast separate subject and text cleanly.
typography: Two short lines, four words: black IT'S YOU and red FEEL THIS in thin rounded capitals. The words stay legible at 160x90 though they are light beside the heavy dark figure; the caption supplies the viewpoint the title only implies with POV.
colors: Near-black navy gear on a white field with a red FEEL THIS line, a red selector detail and a white vest label. The red words signal threat and urgency; saturation is otherwise low and contrast is strong.
psychology: The figure's face is fully covered by the mask and goggles so no expression is visible; the aimed weapon and the red command text read as a threat and authority cue directed at the viewer.
partnership: The title is POV: You're Every Rank In SWAT; the thumbnail adds a single armed officer and the words It's you, so it complements the title by showing one rank rather than every rank. The unanswered question is which ranks follow.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black helmeted figure and gun first, then the red FEEL THIS, then the curved arrow, then the white SWAT label.
art: Detailed cartoon-realistic illustration with consistent outlines and a crisp highlight on the helmet; the gun, vest and gloves are coherent. The plain white background makes the dark subject survive at small sizes.
strength: A strong silhouette on white with red-versus-black text makes the POV hook readable at a glance.
weakness: The caption is thin and small beside the heavy figure, and the single rank shown does not signal the every-rank progression.
bottleneck: Nothing in the image hints at multiple ranks, so the title's hierarchy promise is carried only by words.
action: Hypothesis: add two smaller officers in different gear behind the main figure to test whether showing a rank progression strengthens the every-rank promise.
counterexample: Seq 12 uses the same every-rank title format with a tattooed figure and a text hook, adding visible identity detail where this has a covered face.

composition: The logo is the large central focal point on a diagonal, and the red line runs along the same diagonal to the lower right, linking it to the cartoon character. The text sits low left. The dark background has a soft grey gradient at right behind the face.
typography: Three words in thick white sentence case in two lines at the bottom left, with Enron Scandal spanning about two thirds of the width. The text stays readable at 160x90 and supplies the company and event names that the title withholds.
colors: Black and charcoal background with a bright red declining line, white text, and red, green and blue logo bars. The red line signals loss and decline; colours are saturated against a dark ground for strong contrast.
psychology: The character has wide eyes, an open mouth and both hands pressed to the sides of his head with a ?! marker, a shocked and confused look. The falling line adds a loss cue.
partnership: The title teases a 63 billion dollar company that sold nothing without naming it; the thumbnail names Enron and the scandal, which complements the title but reveals the subject. The unanswered question is how nothing was sold.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the tilted logo first, then the red falling line, then the white Enron Scandal text, then the shocked cartoon face.
art: A 3D-rendered style logo composited with a flat-outline cartoon and a vector chart line; the style mix is visible but coherent because the dark backdrop unifies it. The logo's bevel lighting differs from the flat character, an intentional mismatch rather than an artefact.

scene: A grey-bearded, grey-haired cartoon man in round glasses, an argyle sweater vest and a tie sits on a wooden stool at left with wide eyes, an open mouth and three blue sweat drops beside his head. He holds a calculator whose tiny screen reads ERROR - OVERDRAFT. A curved green arrow above the calculator points back toward the man from the headline. Text fills the right half.
mechanism: A visibly alarmed retiree reading an overdraft error on a calculator turns a spending-categories list into a money-stress story, with the headline promising a place where the money goes.
composition: The seated man occupies the left third and the stacked headline the right two thirds, with the green arrow bridging them at the top. The calculator is the secondary focal point near the centre. A plain white ground keeps the layout clear, though the stool legs and sweater pattern add some line density.
typography: Four words in three lines, with huge black MOST and HERE, white RETIREES in a red box, and a smaller black SPEND. All survive at 160x90. The text restates the title's retiree-spending idea and leaves out the (Wait For #4) teaser.
colors: Black, white and red headline blocks beside a muted blue-and-burgundy sweater, with a green arrow and a red box accent. The red label box reads as emphasis and urgency; contrast against the white ground is very strong.
psychology: The man shows wide round eyes, a gaping mouth and sweat drops, a visible panic cue, while the OVERDRAFT error on the calculator adds a financial-fear cue. The older appearance and the RETIREES label tie the worry to the target age group.
partnership: The title promises the major spending areas for retirees and a hidden fourth item; the thumbnail repeats the retirees-spend idea and adds a distressed man with an overdraft error, which complements the title. The unanswered question is where exactly the money goes, since HERE points at nothing specific.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the giant black MOST first, then the red RETIREES box, then the man's panicked face and calculator, then the green arrow and the word HERE.
art: Clean flat cartoon with thick outlines and a consistent palette; the man's proportions and the stool read coherently. The calculator's small screen text is only legible at full size, and the white background keeps the whole image uncluttered.
strength: A huge three-tier headline with a clear emotional character makes the audience and the money angle obvious at once.
weakness: HERE has no visible target, and the arrow points back at the man rather than at a spending category.
bottleneck: The word HERE promises a reveal that the image does not show.
action: Hypothesis: replace SPEND HERE with a pictured category icon, such as a house or a pill bottle, at the arrow tip to test whether a concrete target improves the promise.

text: DRINK WATER / THIS WAY / STOP URINATING / AT NIGHT!
scene: An older woman with wavy grey hair, round glasses and a pearl-style earring, in a navy cable-knit cardigan, holds a clear glass of water to her mouth with both hands; her eyes look up and to the left over the rim. A dark-red curved arrow runs from the end of THIS WAY to her face and the glass. The background is solid black.
mechanism: A how-to drinking action paired with a night-time outcome claim promises a specific behavioural fix for a common night-time problem.
composition: The headline stack fills the left two thirds in four lines, and the woman with the glass fills the right third as a diagonal subject from the lower right to the upper right. The glass and hands are the secondary focus. Black negative space isolates both text and subject.
typography: Eight words in four lines: two yellow lines, then STOP URINATING in white on a red box, then white AT NIGHT!. The whole stack reads at 160x90, and the red-boxed line is the strongest contrast. The text adds the stop-at-night outcome, while the title adds the urologist label and the over-60 age marker.
colors: Black ground with yellow and white lettering, a red label box and a navy cardigan. The yellow and red signal urgency; the skin and grey hair stay in muted tones for subject separation.
psychology: The woman shows a calm face with her eyes glancing sideways over the glass, no distress cue; the older appearance and the arrow signal a how-to for her age group. The red-boxed outcome line supplies the urgency.
partnership: The title names a urologist, a how-to drinking tip and the over-60 age; the thumbnail repeats the how-to and the night-time outcome and adds a drinking visual, so they complement. The unanswered question is what the this way method is, and the urologist credential is absent from the image.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow DRINK WATER first, then the red-boxed STOP URINATING, then the dark-red arrow to the glass, then the woman's face.
art: Vector-cartoon style with soft shading and a clear outline; the hands holding the glass are readable, and the glass is semi-transparent against dark. The black ground keeps the layout simple, and the small arrow and glass edge are the finest detail.
strength: A strong colour-coded headline hierarchy pairs an action with a benefit in plain words.
weakness: The red-boxed claim reads as a cure for a symptom, and the face is calm with no emotional pull beyond the headline.
bottleneck: Nothing visible shows what this way means, so the how-to promise rests on words only.
action: Hypothesis: replace STOP URINATING with a softer phrase such as FEWER NIGHT TRIPS and add a small clock icon to test whether a milder claim keeps the hook.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses the same black-red-yellow senior-health palette but leads with a body-damage threat instead of a how-to benefit.
medical_notes: A stop-at-night outcome tied to a single drinking method reads like a cure claim, and the urologist credential from the title is not visible on the image.

typography: One orange word with a dark outline in small capitals near the lower middle, only a fraction of the column width. At 160x90 it is a faint dash, so the label disappears and the title's complaining-gut framing carries the idea.
colors: Salmon-pink organ against pale blue hospital tones, an orange caption and dark muted side bars. The warm organ separates from the cool bed and wall; no warning colour is used.
psychology: The face shows narrowed eyes, strongly lowered brows and bared teeth, an intense anger-like cue, while the hospital bed and IV add a sickness cue. Overall the cues point to a fun, exaggerated character rather than a threat.
partnership: The title says the gut is complaining about constipation; the thumbnail shows an angry organ in a hospital bed with the word CONSTIPATED, so it dramatises the same idea and complements the title. The hospital setting hints at severity that the title does not state.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the angry face on the organ first, then the raised fists, then the hospital bed and monitor, then the small orange caption.
art: Polished 3D-render look with glossy specular highlights, soft depth of field and consistent lighting; the organ's gloved fists and arms are coherent. The side bars are an enlarged blurred duplicate of the same frame, a pillarbox fill rather than extra content.

scene: A detailed illustration of a tan, wrinkled dog with its head tipped back and mouth wide open showing teeth and a long tongue, with strings and droplets of drool flying off, a bloodshot eye with tears streaming down the cheek and a brown leather collar on a chain at left. Raw red patches show on the neck beneath and beside the collar. A thin curved arrow from the handwritten text points down-left at the drooling tongue. The background is plain white.
mechanism: A drooling, tearful, collared dog paired with an unsourced large-number caption makes the title's nightmare claim feel like widespread suffering.
composition: The dog's head and neck fill the left two thirds on a diagonal that rises to the nose, with the mouth as the main focal point. The text block sits at upper right with a small arrow into the drool. White space on the right gives strong separation and the layout is simple.
typography: Four words in two lines, a large 10 million above a smaller suffers daily in thin black handwriting. The words are legible at 160x90 but light in weight beside the dark illustration. The text adds a statistic that the title does not state, though it does not say what is being counted.
colors: Tan and brown dog with red raw patches, a dark brown collar and white ground. The red patches and tears are the only bright accents; the overall palette is earthy, with strong subject-to-ground contrast.
psychology: The dog's head is thrown back with a wide-open mouth, a bloodshot tearing eye and flying drool, a visibly distressed pose. The raw neck patches and collar add a vulnerability cue.
partnership: The title calls being born a dog a nightmare and promises something nobody tells you; the thumbnail adds the 10 million daily-suffering figure and a distressed dog, so it complements the title. The unanswered question is what is being counted, since the number has no stated source or subject.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the open drooling mouth first, then the 10 million text, then the bloodshot eye, then the collar and chain.
art: Detailed illustrated style with hatching, skin folds and flying droplets drawn consistently; the collar, chain and wrinkles hold together. The white ground keeps it uncluttered at mobile size.
strength: A large distressed dog face with a short statistic gives a strong emotive hook with an uncluttered layout.
weakness: The statistic is unsourced and unclear about what is counted, and the thin handwriting has less weight than the graphic gore.
bottleneck: The number lacks a subject, so it reads as a vague claim that reduces credibility.
action: Hypothesis: change the caption to name the subject such as 10 MILLION DOGS in heavier lettering to test whether a clear statistic reads as more credible.
counterexample: Seq 3 shares the white-ground, distressed-animal-head, handwritten-caption layout, but its caption names a symptom while this one gives a statistic.
expression_label: head thrown back, open mouth, tearing bloodshot eye
